meta.principle: Document first. Interpretation second. Counter-evidence always visible.

nodes.title: Joop Westerweel
nodes.summary: Dutch teacher, pacifist and resistance organizer. He helped Jews and young Palestine Pioneers hide and escape. He was executed at Kamp Vught on 11 August 1944.
nodes.question: What does protection demand when law itself has become persecution?

media.label: NM Kamp Vught video/podcast with Bart Westerweel

nodes.title: Sant’Anna di Stazzema
nodes.summary: On 12 August 1944, civilians in Sant’Anna di Stazzema and nearby hamlets were massacred by German SS troops with fascist collaborators. The site later became a National Park of Peace.
nodes.question: How can a place of massacre become a place that teaches peace without erasing what happened?
nodes.imageCredit: Musei Provincia di Lucca — Ossuary Memorial

nodes.title: The machinery of deportation
nodes.summary: August 1942 shows persecution becoming logistics: ghettos, transports, administrative coordination and deportation. Rymanów and Radom are used here as documented case windows, not as symbols for all experiences.
nodes.question: At what point does bureaucracy become participation in violence?

sources.label: USHMM — Days of Remembrance in Rymanów

nodes.title: Maximilian Kolbe
nodes.summary: Kolbe volunteered to take the place of Franciszek Gajowniczek, who had been selected for death by starvation. Kolbe was killed by poison injection on 14 August 1941 in Block 11.
nodes.question: What makes an act of sacrifice morally luminous without turning suffering into spectacle?

nodes.title: 15 August — Netherlands remembers
nodes.summary: The Netherlands commemorates the end of the Second World War for the Kingdom and victims of the war against Japan and the Japanese occupation of the former Dutch East Indies. The Indisch Monument in The Hague includes a bronze memorial bell.
nodes.question: How does public remembrance become something a later generation can inherit rather than merely observe?

nodes.title: Brother Roger · Białystok
nodes.summary: Two distinct memories are kept side by side, not merged: Jewish armed resistance during the liquidation of the Białystok ghetto in 1943, and the life of Brother Roger of Taizé, killed during evening prayer on 16 August 2005 after a life devoted to reconciliation and solidarity.
nodes.question: When does protecting life call for resistance, and when does healing call for reconciliation?

sources.label: Yad Vashem — armed resistance in Białystok

nodes.title: The name and the lie
nodes.summary: On 17 August 1938 Nazi Germany imposed additional names, Israel for many Jewish men and Sara for many Jewish women, as an administrative marker. On 17 August 1921 The Times published Philip Graves’s exposure of the plagiarism behind the antisemitic Protocols forgery.
nodes.question: How do labels make persecution easier — and what does rigorous source-checking do to a weaponized lie?
